steps.response:
The provided image is a lateral chest X-ray. Assessing cardiomegaly (enlarged heart) is primarily done on a frontal (PA or AP) view by measuring the cardiothoracic ratio. On a lateral view, one looks for the posterior cardiac border extending significantly behind the inferior vena cava line or occupying excessive retrosternal space, but "mild" vs "severe" is difficult to quantify definitively without a frontal view. However, looking at the lateral projection, the cardiac silhouette appears somewhat prominent but not massively enlarged to the point of being obviously "severe". The heart size appears within normal limits or perhaps mildly enlarged given the projection, but certainly not severe. Let's use an expert tool to confirm the visual assessment of the cardiac size on this lateral view.
